To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
actual air pollution, perceived air pollution, and environmental transparency are all significantly related to each other in a multilevel context.
actual air pollution and environmental transparency are positively associated with perceived air pollution in China.
the relationship between actual air pollution and perceived air pollution is moderated by environmental transparency. (C) 2017 The Authors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of environmental transparency and the relationship between perceived and actual air pollution.
the role of transparency in environmental governance.
the environmental transparency of local governments in China, which has not yet been studied in previous research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
environmental transparency is a crucial factor in the relationship between actual perceived air pollution.

environmental transparency is important to the relationship between perceived and actual air pollution, and that the relationship is more complicated than what has been previously assumed in developed countries.

the perception of air pollution is more or less in congruence with the actual air pollution, but environmental transparency is an important factor that can affect people's perception of air pollution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the environmental governance of a country should not only be evaluated by the actual environmental quality of the country but also by its environmental transparency.

the environmental transparency of local governments is crucial to the public perception of air pollution and that the public perception of pollution can be used to evaluate the performance of local governments.
environmental transparency can help improve the quality of the environment in China.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between environmental transparency and air pollution in developing countries is not a one-way street but a two-way street.
the environmental governance system should not only focus on the reduction of air pollution but also on the transparency of environmental information.
environmental transparency can help improve the quality of environmental information, which in turn can help improve the public's perception of environmental quality.
